audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on all seven rows: full says Yasuo 7/7 at HARD 8/10, content win[] says Akshan 7/7 with whys to match. Every phase why-text also described Akshan winning under a Yasuo side.
audit.why: 48.28% over 2500 games and a champion whose W deletes Akshan's entire damage pattern for four seconds. The full layer's HARD read is right; the content layer was never updated.
audit.corrected: win[0..6] all flip to Yasuo, whys rewritten to say why, and the phase why-texts rewritten to match their sides.
sources: currentText full phases[].side vs content win[]

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes framed Akshan's first lethality item as a way to 'kill him through Wind Wall', and framed level 6 as Akshan's window.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for its full 4 seconds — Akshan's autos, Avengerang, the swing's shots and Comeuppance's bullets are all projectiles, so there is nothing to stagger through. Last Breath is 70/50/30 and Yasuo supplies his own knockup.
audit.corrected: Yasuo spikes at 3 (Wind Wall) and on crit items; Akshan's only spike is Wind Wall's 21 seconds of downtime.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json W text and blocksProjectiles flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Two false interactions: that Wind Wall 'can only block one instance', and that Yasuo gets his Last Breath knockup 'off your own E return' / 'your own Heroic Swing boomerang'.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks ALL enemy projectiles for 4 seconds. Akshan has no knockup or displacement anywhere in his kit — the airborne source is Yasuo's own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind or an ally's CC. Telling a player their boomerang sets up Last Breath makes them misplay a spell they should be throwing.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall blanks the entire pattern for 4s on a 25s cooldown; Last Breath's knockup comes from Yasuo's own double Steel Tempest, never from Akshan.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json — no knockup flag on any slot

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall was tracked all over the page without its cooldown, and Sweeping Blade's recast restriction was never mentioned.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17 for a 4-second wall — that is a countable 21-second window at rank 1. Sweeping Blade cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds, so Yasuo's repeat mobility depends on the minion wave, not on Akshan.
audit.corrected: Numbers added; wave-clump discipline framed as denying dash targets.

edits.before: Last Breath becomes dangerous only if he lands a knockup, whether from his own E off a minion or your own Heroic Swing boomerang — be careful not to set him up for free. Comeuppance gives you a strong answer if he tries an aggressive dive, letting you turn the tables since he has no way to escape your ranged execute.
edits.after: Last Breath only works off an airborne target, and the source is his own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind or an ally's CC — nothing in your kit gives him one, so the danger is his setup, not yours. Comeuppance answers a dive, but every bullet is a projectile: never start the channel while Wind Wall is up or the whole ult is eaten.

notes: This matchup shipped with the level chart fully inverted between layers — full had Yasuo 7/7 at HARD 8/10, content had Akshan 7/7 with Akshan-favoured whys, and the full layer's own why-texts described Akshan winning under Yasuo sides. All three are now aligned to the Yasuo read that the 48.28% win rate and the kit support. Two fabricated interactions removed: that Wind Wall blocks only one instance (it blocks all projectiles for 4s) and that Akshan's Heroic Swing or Avengerang return supplies a knockup for Last Breath (Akshan has no displacement at all). Added the interaction the page most needed: Comeuppance's bullets are projectiles, so a Wind Wall on the release eats a 100-second ultimate. tldr and winCon were already Yasuo-specific and good; breakdown.early, breakdown.mid, breakdown.wave, breakdown.late, ahead, tradeGood and tradeBad remain shared Akshan boilerplate.
